title: Blest Are the Souls That Hear and Know
description: Blest Are the Souls That Hear and Know in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 89, part 4, headed “A blessed gospel”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Blest are the souls that hear and know The go-spel's joy-ful sound; Peace shall at-tend the path they go, And light their steps sur-round.

lines: Blest are the souls that hear and know
Peace shall attend the path they go,
Their joy shall bear their spirits up
The Lord, our glory and defence,
Israel, thy king for ever reigns,

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
